This topic covers how to configure and manage various PDF templates within the ERP system, including setting up different layouts, associating templates with specific courses, and understanding the default template mechanism for documents like ID cards, certificates, and receipts.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the PDF Template section.
2. Click on the option to add a new template.
3. Select the type of template (e.g., Fee Receipt, ID Card, Character Certificate).
4. Provide a unique name for the template.
5. Choose the desired print layout (e.g., Single, Two Horizontal, Two Vertical, Four).
6. Optionally, associate the template with specific courses or classes if different designs are required.
7. Select a default template from the available backend options or load an existing one.
8. Review the template preview for design and layout.
9. Use the 'Default' toggle to activate or deactivate the template for use.

Business Rules:
• The system prints the template *attached to the trigger* (the document type selected for printing), regardless of the code content within the template.
• If multiple templates are set as 'Default' for the same trigger and class, the system will print the first one in the series.
• Templates can be customized per class/course.
• The 'Default' toggle activates (on) or deactivates (off) a template for printing.
• If no existing template is defaulted on, the backend default template will be printed.

Important Notes:
• Always verify the template code to ensure it matches the intended document type to avoid printing incorrect documents (e.g., a bona fide certificate instead of a fee receipt).
• The preview function is primarily for design verification and may not reflect the final printed output perfectly, especially if there are unclosed HTML tags or structural errors in the code.
• Most default templates might require minor code adjustments to meet specific requirements.
• Complex reports (e.g., advanced report cards) often require fully customized design and coding.
• Styling (e.g., uppercase) can be applied using HTML elements like 'div', 'span', or 'x-transform' within the template code.

question: How do I load an existing template for customization?
answer:
This topic provides guidance on customizing PDF templates by modifying their underlying code and using dynamic variables. It also covers essential debugging techniques to identify and correct issues with missing or incorrect data in printed templates.

Steps:
1. **Load Template**: Select the desired template type (e.g., Character Certificate) and click "Load Template" to retrieve its existing code.
2. **Modify Code**: Edit the template's HTML/CSS code. For example, to make text uppercase, apply `text-transform: uppercase;` styling to the relevant `div`, `span`, or `x-transform` element.
3. **Identify Variables**: Use variables to display dynamic data. Common variables include: `DisplayData.EntityName` (Institute Name), `DisplayData.EntityAddress` (Institute Address), `DisplayData.StudentName` (Student's Name), `DisplayData.FatherName` (Student's Father's Name), `DisplayData.Category` (Student's Category), `DisplayData.Session` (Academic Session), `DisplayData.Logo` (School/Institute Logo).
4. **Debug Missing Data**: If a variable's data is not printing: Print the document (even if data is missing). Right-click on the page and select "Inspect". Navigate to the "Console" tab in the developer tools. Locate and expand the `object` (or relevant array) to view all available variables and their exact names. Compare the variable name used in your template code with the exact name found in the console. Correct any discrepancies in the template code (e.g., change `DisplayData.StudentCategory` to `DisplayData.Category` if that's what the console shows).

Business Rules:
• All variables must be prefixed with `DisplayData.` (e.g., `DisplayData.VariableName`). `DisplayData` acts as an array that calls and retrieves the data.
• The exact variable name as displayed in the browser's console must be used for data to populate correctly.
• For complex reports like report cards, variables might be nested within arrays (e.g., for columns, fee heads, skill groups, subjects, assessment groups).

Important Notes:
• Most default templates may require minor code adjustments to meet specific requirements.
• Some templates, especially for advanced report cards or specific certificates (e.g., custom transfer certificates), may require extensive custom coding and design.
• The console is a critical tool for debugging and identifying the correct variable names and data structures.

• The 'Preview' function is primarily for checking the design and code, not the final print output. Unclosed HTML tags or incorrect code can prevent a proper preview.
• Most default templates provided by the system may require minor code adjustments to meet specific institutional requirements.

question: How do I add a new PDF template in the ERP system?
answer:
This topic covers the process of setting up and managing various PDF templates within the ERP system, including ID cards, certificates, receipts, and admission forms. It details how to add new templates, configure print layouts, associate templates with specific courses or schools, and manage default settings.

Steps:

4. Provide a unique name for the template.
5. Configure the print count and layout: "One" for a single print, "Two with Horizontal" for two prints horizontally, "Two as Vertical" for two prints vertically (one below the other), or "Four" for four prints (divided into four sections).

• The system prints the template specifically attached to a particular trigger, regardless of the code content. For example, if a "Fee Receipt" trigger is linked to a "Bona Fide Certificate" template, printing a fee receipt will result in a bona fide certificate.
• If a template's "Default" toggle is "On", that template will be printed.
• If a template's "Default" toggle is "Off", the previously active template will be printed.
• If no existing template is defaulted "On", the back-end default template will be used.
• If multiple templates are defaulted "On" for the same trigger (e.g., multiple student ID cards for the same class), the first one in the series will be printed.
• Certificates can be different for respective classes or schools.

Important Notes:
• The preview function is for checking design, layout, and code, but it is not the final print.
• Always verify the template code and its associated trigger to ensure the correct document is printed.
• Default templates often suffice for standard requirements; customization is typically for advanced or specific needs.
• Ensure all HTML tags (e.g., `div`, `section`) are properly closed in the template code to avoid rendering issues during preview or printing.

question: Why is the wrong certificate printing when I click 'Print Fee Receipt'?
answer:
This topic explains the critical concept that the ERP system prints a template based on the trigger (the action initiated by the user, e.g., 'Print Fee Receipt'), not necessarily the name or code assigned to the template itself. Steps:
1. When configuring a template, locate the 'Default' toggle.

• The template associated with a specific trigger (e.g., 'Print Fee Receipt' button) will be printed, regardless of the template's name or internal code, if that trigger is hard-linked to a specific template.
• If multiple templates are defaulted ON for the same trigger/context, the system will print the first one in the series (based on internal code logic).
• If a template is defaulted ON, it will be printed. If it's defaulted OFF, the previously active template will be printed. If no template is defaulted ON, a backend default template will be used.

Important Notes:
• Always verify the code and the trigger association to ensure the correct template is printed.
• A common mistake is selecting a 'Fee Receipt' template type but linking it to a 'Bonafide Certificate' code, resulting in a bonafide certificate printing when a fee receipt is requested.

• For some specific cases (e.g., ID cards for different schools), multiple defaults might be allowed.

question: How do I configure a new vendor API for tracking?
answer:
Track Config is used to set up the details of a vendor's API for vehicle tracking. This involves defining the API URL, the HTTP method (GET or POST), any necessary query parameters, and request headers. It also includes specifying the GPS ID Key which the backend uses to match ERP vehicle IDs with the vendor's system.

Steps:
1. **API URL:** Copy the base API URL from the vendor's documentation. This is typically the part of the URL before any query parameters (i.e., before the first '?').
2. **Method:** Select the appropriate HTTP method (GET or POST) based on the vendor's API configuration. GET is used when query parameters are attached to the URL, while POST is used for sending data in an object (request body).
3. **Query Parameters:** Add any required query parameters, such as authentication tokens or additional values needed to call the API. For example, `token=your_token_value`. The GPS ID Key (e.g., 'wickle number') is also configured here to pass the ERP vehicle's GPS ID to the vendor API.
4. **Headers:** Configure request headers, such as `Accept` with a value of `application/json`, to specify the expected response format.
5. **Request Body:** (Applicable for POST requests only) Configure the data object to be sent in the request body.

Business Rules:
• The choice between GET and POST methods depends entirely on how the vendor has configured their API.
• The setup for Track Config is a one-time configuration on the backend; the app will automatically call the configured API based on this setup.
• The GPS ID Key in Track Config is the parameter name (e.g., 'wickle number') that the vendor's API expects to receive the vehicle's unique ID.

Important Notes:
• Query patterns are values attached after a '?' in the URL.
• The 'Test Connection' feature allows verifying the API configuration and viewing the raw response, but it may have UI issues and might not always work as expected on the portal.

question: How do I configure the ERP system to understand a vendor's API response?
answer:
Response Config defines how the ERP system should parse and interpret the data received from a vendor's tracking API. This involves specifying the path to the list of tracking data within the JSON response, as well as the unique keys for matching vehicles, latitude, longitude, and speed.

Steps:
1. **List Path Key:** Identify the JSON path where the list (array) of tracking data is located in the vendor's API response (e.g., `data.list`). Use dot notation to access nested arrays.
2. **Match Key:** Specify the unique key within each item of the response list that identifies a specific vehicle (e.g., `wickle key`). This key is used to match the response data to the correct vehicle in the ERP system.
3. **Latitude Key:** Enter the key from the vendor's response that contains the latitude value.
4. **Longitude Key:** Enter the key from the vendor's response that contains the longitude value.
5. **Speed Key:** Enter the key from the vendor's response that contains the speed value.

Business Rules:
• The `Match Key` in Response Config is the key within the vendor's response that uniquely identifies a vehicle, which may be different from the `GPS ID Key` used in Track Config to send the ID.
• The `List Path Key` helps the system navigate the JSON response to find the relevant array of tracking data.

Important Notes:
• The vendor's API response structure (which keys to use) will be provided in documentation or determined by inspecting the response via tools like Postman.
• If the 'Test Connection' feature in Track Config is not working on the portal, the API response should first be verified using Postman to determine the correct keys for Response Config.

question: How do I configure the API URL in Track Config?
answer:
Track Config is used to define the details of a vendor's API, including the API URL, HTTP method (GET/POST), query parameters for additional values like tokens, and headers for specifying response formats.

Steps:
1. **API URL**: Copy the base API URL (the part before any '?' query patterns) and paste it into the 'API URL' field.
2. **Method**: Select the appropriate HTTP method (GET or POST).
3. **Query Parameters**: If the API requires values to be appended after a '?' in the URL (e.g., tokens, extra values), add them here in 'key=value' format.
4. **Headers**: Specify headers for the API call. For example, to receive a JSON response, input 'Accept' as the key and 'application/json' as the value.
5. **Request Body**: If the method is POST, add the request body in an object format (key-value pairs).

Business Rules:
• GET method is used when query patterns are sent in the URL.
• POST method is used when data is sent in an object (request body).
• Query patterns are attached after a '?' in the API URL.
• The setup is performed once; the backend automatically calls the vendor API based on this configuration.

Important Notes:
• Ensure the API URL is copied correctly, excluding query patterns.
• The 'token' or other extra values for query parameters should be copied exactly as provided.

question: How do I set up the API URL and method in Track Config?
answer:
Track Config defines how the ERP system calls a vendor's tracking API, including the API URL, HTTP method, query parameters, request headers, and the key used to identify the vehicle.

Steps:
1. Identify the full API URL from the vendor's documentation.
2. Copy the part of the URL *before* any question marks ('?') into the 'API URL' field.
3. Select the appropriate 'Method': 'GET' (for query parameters) or 'POST' (for request body).
4. For 'Query Parameters': Add any required tokens or extra values as key-value pairs (e.g., 'token=your_token_value').
5. For 'Headers': Add 'Accept' as the key and 'application/json' as the value to ensure JSON response format.
6. For 'Request Body' (if Method is POST): Define the data to be sent in an object format (e.g., '{"vehicleId": "V123"}').
7. For 'GPS ID Key': Copy the 'matching key' from the vendor's documentation (e.g., 'vehicle number') and paste it into this field. This key will be used by the backend to pass our internal vehicle ID to the vendor API.

Business Rules:
• The part of the URL before '?' is considered the base API URL.
• Query patterns are data appended after '?' in a GET request.
• Object-based data transmission is typically a POST request.
• The 'Request Body' is only applicable for 'POST' requests.
• The 'GPS ID Key' is the parameter name that the vendor API expects for the vehicle identifier.

Important Notes:
• This setup is performed once for each vendor API.
• The backend automatically uses this configuration when the app calls its own API.
• The token value in query parameters is a stream that needs to be copied exactly.
• The 'GPS ID Key' is what *we send* to the vendor API.

question: What fields are required when creating a new inventory item?
answer:
This process outlines how to create a new item in the inventory system. It involves entering item details, assigning the item to an existing item group, and the option to create a new item group if the required one does not exist.

Steps:
1. Click on 'Create' in the Item Masters section.
2. Enter the Item Code (optional).
3. Enter the Item Name (e.g., 'erasers').
4. Select the Item Group (e.g., 'stationary data', 'instrument').
5. If the required Item Group does not exist, click the icon to create a new Item Group.
6. Enter the new Item Group name.
7. Select 'Primary' or an existing parent group (e.g., 'pens' under 'stationary data').
8. Save the new Item Group.
9. Save the new Item.

Business Rules:
• The Item Code field is non-mandatory.
• Every item must be assigned to an Item Group.
• Item Groups can be nested (e.g., 'ball pens' under 'pens', and 'pens' under 'stationary data').

Important Notes:
• Item codes can be used to differentiate between similar items (e.g., two types of erasers).
• The system allows for the creation of new item groups directly from the item creation interface if needed.

question: How do I create a new inventory item in the system?
answer:
This topic covers the process of creating, viewing, and editing items within the inventory module. It explains how to define item codes, assign items to groups, and manage item group hierarchies. Users can also create new item groups on the fly if needed.

Steps:
1. To create a new item: Navigate to Inventory > Masters > Items, then click 'Create'.
2. Enter the Item Code (optional).
3. Enter the Item Name (e.g., Erasers).
4. Select an existing Item Group (e.g., Stationary Data, Instrument).
5. If the desired Item Group does not exist, click the icon to create a new one.
6. When creating an Item Group, specify if it's 'Primary' (top-level) or a sub-group under an existing group (e.g., 'Pens' under 'Stationary Data').
7. Save the item.
8. To view or edit an existing item: Navigate to Inventory > Masters > Items, then click 'Edit'. Search for the item and make necessary modifications.

Business Rules:
• The Item Code field is non-mandatory.
• Item groups can be organized hierarchically (e.g., 'Ball Pens' under 'Pens', and 'Pens' under 'Stationary Data').

Important Notes:
• The system allows users to create new item groups directly from the item creation interface if they are not already present.

question: How do I transfer stock between different stores?
answer:
This topic explains the process of transferring inventory items from one store or department to another within the ERP system. It is typically used to distribute items purchased and stored centrally to various operational departments or branches.

Steps:
1. Navigate to Inventory > Transactions > Stock Transfer.
2. Select the 'Source Store' (e.g., Central Store) from which items are being transferred.
3. Select the 'Destination Store' or department to which items are being transferred.
4. Enter the 'Date' of the stock transfer.
5. Select the 'Item' to be transferred.
6. Enter the 'Quantity' of the item being transferred.
7. Add a 'Narration' or reason for the transfer.
8. Optionally, upload 'Additional Documents' related to the transfer.
9. Save the stock transfer entry.

Business Rules:
• Stock transfers move items between defined stores or departments.
• A reason or narration should be provided for each transfer.

Important Notes:
• This function is crucial for managing inventory distribution across multiple locations or departments (e.g., from a main store to teaching departments).

question: How do I add a new inventory item to the system?
answer:
This topic covers the creation and management of core inventory master data, including individual items (e.g., tables, pens), their units of measure (e.g., liters, pieces), and how to categorize them using item groups (e.g., stationary data, instruments). It also explains how to create hierarchical item groups.

Steps:
1. To Create a New Item:
2. 1. Navigate to the Item creation interface (e.g., click 'create').
3. 2. Enter the Item Name (e.g., 'erasers').
4. 3. (Optional) Enter an Item Code (non-mandatory).
5. 4. Select an existing Item Group (e.g., 'stationary data').
6. 5. If the required Item Group does not exist, click the icon to create a new one.
7. 6. Save the item.
8. To Create a New Item Group:
9. 1. Access the Item Group creation interface (e.g., via an icon during item creation).
10. 2. Enter the Item Group Name (e.g., 'stationary data').
11. 3. Specify if it's a primary group or a sub-group under an existing group.
12. 4. Save the item group.
13. To View/Edit Existing Items:
14. 1. Navigate to the Item management section.
15. 2. Click 'edit' or 'cross edit' for an existing item.
16. 3. Use the search functionality to find specific items.

Business Rules:
• Items must be assigned a unit of measure (e.g., liters for chemicals, pieces for erasers, numbers for furniture).
• Item groups can be organized hierarchically (e.g., 'ball pens' under 'pens', and 'pens' under 'stationary data').

Important Notes:
• The Item Code field is non-mandatory.
• New item groups can be created on-the-fly if they don't exist.
• If you want to keep a main store, you have to keep a segment.
• If you want to keep an institute, you have to have two branches in the same panel.

question: How do I print a student's Transfer Certificate (TC)?
answer:
Explains how to generate and print various student certificates (e.g., DC Certificate, Tuition Fee Certificate, Character Certificate, Appreciation Certificate) and ID cards. It covers searching for individual students, entering specific details for certificates, saving, printing, and also provides an option for bulk printing.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Student Certificates'.
2. Select the desired certificate type (e.g., DC Certificate, Tuition Fee Certificate, Character Certificate, Student ID Card, Admit Card, Appreciation Certificate).
3. For a single student, search by name or use the available filter options.
4. Enter any required details specific to the certificate being generated.
5. Click 'Save' to store the certificate data.
6. Click 'Print' to generate a physical copy of the certificate.
7. For bulk printing, select multiple students from the list.
8. Choose the 'Bulk Print' option for the desired certificate type (e.g., ID cards, character certificates, appreciation certificates).

Business Rules:
• The 'Print and Inactive' option can be used when a student is being released, allowing for simultaneous certificate printing and status change.
• DC Certificates are typically used for student release.
• Student Ledger and Tuition Fee Certificates are related to financial records.
• Character Certificates are often required for college admissions or transfers.

Important Notes:
• The system supports both single and bulk printing of various certificates and ID cards.
• The layout and content of printed certificates (e.g., DC certificate) can be configured.

question: What is the difference between an 'active' and 'inactive' student record?
answer:

Steps:
1. Identify a student whose status needs to be managed.
2. A student is conceptually set to 'Inactive' if their admission is canceled or they are no longer present in the institute for the current session.

Business Rules:
• A student becomes 'Inactive' if their admission is canceled (e.g., non-payment of fees, leaving the institute).
• An 'Active' student is currently enrolled in the session.

question: How can I view a list of all students in the ERP system?
answer:
Explains how to view a comprehensive list of all students, adjust the number of records displayed per page, and apply filters to search for specific student data based on criteria such as class, section, fee category (e.g., General, RTE 134A), and student status (Old/New).

Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Student' module.
2. Click on 'Student List'.
3. View the data of all students present in the institute.
4. To adjust the number of students displayed per screen, modify the 'item bar page' setting (e.g., set to 25).
5. To filter the student list, click on the 'Filter' option.
6. Select desired criteria such as 'Class' (e.g., Nursery), 'Section', 'Fee Category' (e.g., General, RTE 134A), or 'Student Status' (Old/New).
7. Unselect any categories not needed for filtering.
8. Click 'Filter' to apply the selected criteria and narrow down the list.

Business Rules:
• RTE 134A is a specific fee category for students who may not pay fees due to government provisions.
• 'Old' and 'New' distinguish students based on their enrollment session.

Important Notes:
• The filter option is a common feature available across many screens in the system.
• The 'item bar page' setting directly controls how many records are visible on the screen at once.

question: How do I set the default session for admissions?
answer:
This topic covers various settings related to student admissions, including selecting the default admission session, configuring roll number and admission number generation (auto-generate or use application number), allowing backdated admissions, setting up admission fee receipt numbering, and making counselor calls mandatory.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Preferences' > 'Admissions'.
2. **Select admissions session:** Choose the default academic session for which admissions data will be displayed and processed (e.g., 25-26).
3. **Application data approved auto-generate (Roll Number):**
4.   - 'On': Automatically generates roll numbers for students upon admission.
5.   - 'Off': Roll numbers are not auto-generated; the application number is used as the admission number, and roll numbers are assigned later.
6. **Warn admission number (Auto-generate Admission Number):** Enable this to automatically generate admission numbers.
7. **Allow backdate admission:** Disable this option to prevent users from recording admissions with a past date.
8. **Admission fee receipt number:** Configure whether receipt numbers for admission-related fees (e.g., prospectus fee, entrance fee) are separate for each session.
9. **Counselor compulsory call:** Enable this to make it mandatory for counselors to call applicants as part of the admission process.

Business Rules:
• The choice between auto-generating roll numbers or using application numbers depends on the institute's specific admission process and policy.
• Backdated admissions are generally disabled to maintain data integrity and accurate record-keeping.

Important Notes:
• Carefully consider the roll number generation setting as it impacts the student's unique identifier throughout their academic journey.
• Disabling backdated admissions helps in maintaining accurate and chronological admission records.

question: What is an active session in the ERP?
answer:
Explains how to set and understand the active session in the ERP, which determines the default academic year displayed upon logging in or switching entities.

Steps:
1. Navigate to "Institute Setup".
2. Go to "Session Setup".
3. Locate the desired session in the list.
4. Click the star icon (labeled "Active Session") next to the session in the 'Action' column.
5. Save the changes.

Business Rules:
• The active session is the default session that opens when you log in or switch to a specific entity.
• Only one session can be marked as active at a time for an entity.

Important Notes:
• Even if multiple sessions exist, only the active one will open by default.
• Users can manually switch to other sessions if needed, but the active session is the system's default.

question: How do I add custom fields to a student's profile?
answer:
This topic explains how to configure student fields, including applying default fields, adding custom fields, and defining their properties such as display name, visibility, group, and data type. It also mentions the capability for bulk import and delete of student data.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Student fields'.
2. Click 'Click here to apply default' to automatically add standard student fields.
3. To add a new custom field, click 'Add new fields'.
4. Define the 'Display Name' for the custom field (e.g., 'Sport Certificate Count').
5. Choose whether to 'Hide' the field if it's for internal use only and should not be visible to all users.
6. Assign the field to a 'Group' (e.g., 'Personal Details') for better organization within the student profile.
7. Select the appropriate 'Field Type' (e.g., Text, Drop-down, File).
8. Save the changes to apply the new field configuration.

Business Rules:
• Student fields are compulsory for entering and storing student data within the ERP.

question: How do I control which modules are visible on the student mobile app?
answer:
This topic details how to configure the student mobile app, controlling which modules (profile, diary, attendance, fees, library, etc.) are visible, and setting up fee payment options, including term selection, fee head visibility, partial payments, and minimum payment percentages.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Preferences' > 'Student app preferences'.
2. **Module Visibility:** Toggle options to control which modules (e.g., Profile, School Diary, Attendance, Fee, Examination, Library) are visible and accessible on the student mobile app.
3. **Mapping of Transactions:** This setting is automatically configured for app payments and typically does not require manual intervention.
4. **Fee Setting for App:** Configure how students can pay fees via the mobile app:
5.   - 'Select a term': Allow students to choose the specific academic session for which they are making fee payments (current or previous).
6.   - 'Show fee head': Enable this to display individual fee heads during the payment process.
7.   - 'Pay full amount or partial': Determine if students are allowed to make partial payments or if they must pay the full outstanding amount.
8.   - 'Select specific fee heads': Allow students to pay for particular fee heads only (e.g., transport fees only).
9.   - 'Flexible module (Minimum Percentage)': Set a minimum percentage of the total fee that a student must pay via the app (e.g., 10% of a 10,000 INR fee). If set to 0, even a nominal amount like 1 INR can be submitted.

Business Rules:
• The 'Flexible module' allows institutes to enforce a minimum payment threshold for app-based fee transactions.

Important Notes:
• Carefully configure module visibility to ensure that students only have access to relevant information and functionalities.
• The fee payment settings directly impact the student's experience and flexibility when making fee payments through the mobile app.

question: How do I promote all students to the next academic session at once?
answer:
Describes how to configure and execute bulk promotion of all eligible students from one academic session to the next, providing a report on the promotion outcome.

Steps:
1. Configuration
2. Execution
3. Reporting

Business Rules:
• Bulk promotion operates based on the configurations defined in "Student Session Management Config".
• The 'To Category' for all promoted students is always "Old".
• For schools, "Promoted with Dues" is typically preferred; for colleges, "Simple Promote" is common. This choice must be confirmed with the client.
• If sections are to be combined during promotion (e.g., Class 1A and 1B to Class 2A), this must be confirmed by the institute.
• Inactive students are automatically excluded from bulk promotion.
• Promotion will be skipped for students if the fee structure for their target class/session is not set up.

Important Notes:
• Bulk promotion is the most efficient method for promoting a large student body.
• The report file provides an overview of the promotion results; for detailed verification, export student data and use tools like VLOOKUP.
• If a single class requires different 'Promoted Status' (with/without dues) for different students, bulk promotion cannot handle this; manual promotion must be used for those specific students.

question: How do I promote a single student to the next academic year?
answer:
Details the process of manually promoting individual or selected groups of students from one academic session and class to the next, with options for handling pending dues.

Steps:
1. Navigate to "Student" -> "Student Session Management".
2. Use the "Filter" option to select the 'From Class' (e.g., Class 1) and 'From Section' (e.g., A) of the students you wish to promote.
3. Select the specific student(s) from the displayed list.
4. Choose the 'To Class' (e.g., Class 2) for the selected students.
5. Click "Add selected student to session".
6. In the pop-up window, verify the 'From Session' (disabled, e.g., 24-25).
7. Select the 'To Session' (e.g., 25-26).
8. Select the 'To Class' (e.g., Class 2) and 'To Section' (e.g., A).
9. Set the 'Category' for the promoted student (typically "Old").
10. Choose the 'Promoted Status': "Simple Promote" (dues remain in current session) or "Promoted with Dues" (pending dues carried forward).
11. Confirm and save the promotion.

Business Rules:
• Only active students can be promoted. Inactive students will be skipped.
• The choice between "Simple Promote" and "Promoted with Dues" should be confirmed by the client/institute as it impacts fee collection.
• Promotion will be skipped if the fee structure for the target class and session is not yet set up.

Important Notes:
• The system will display a message indicating the status of the promotion (e.g., "Student updated", "Skipped", "Re-updated").
• A "Skip" status often indicates a missing fee group for the target class/session.
• Manual promotion is suitable for promoting a small number of students or when specific students require different due handling within the same class.

question: How do teachers provide feedback to students in the ERP system?
answer:
Process for teachers to provide structured feedback for students, including a title, type, category, description, and optional attachments. Feedback can be marked as private or open.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Student Feedback'.
2. Use the filter options to select the specific class or view all classes' data.
3. Select the student for whom feedback is to be given.
4. Enter a 'Feedback Title'.
5. Choose the visibility option: 'Open Private' (visible to other teachers in feedback reports) or 'Private' (visible only to the teacher who gave it).
6. Select the 'Feedback Type' (e.g., Positive, Negative, Neutral) from the dropdown.
7. Select the 'Feedback Category' (e.g., Academic Performance, Sports, Behavior) from the dropdown.
8. Add a detailed 'Feedback Description'.
9. Optionally, upload an 'Attachment File'.
10. Select 'Send Notification' if the feedback should be visible on the student's app.
11. Save the feedback.

Business Rules:
• Feedback types and categories must be pre-configured in 'Institute Setup' before they can be used.
• Students can view their feedback on the student app if the 'Send Notification' option is selected.

Important Notes:
• 'Open Private' feedback is shared among teachers, while 'Private' feedback remains confidential to the giver.
• Feedback provided is recorded on the student's timeline, accessible through their profile.

question: How can I automate the transfer of receipts to accounts?
answer:
This topic describes various automation features and alert configurations, including automating vouchers, payroll, and analytics, enabling OTP verification for gate passes, and setting up automated alerts for due fees and library matters.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Preferences' > 'Automate feature'.
2. **Automate Voucher:** Enable this option to automatically transfer receipts to the accounting system on a daily basis.
3. **Automate Payroll:** Enable this to automate payroll processes, linking them directly to employee salaries.
4. **Automate Analytics:** Enable this to automate the transfer of alerts and data for analytical purposes.
5. **Gate Pass OTP Verification:** Turn this option on to require OTP verification for the issuance of gate passes.
6. **Due Fee Alert:** Configure timely alerts (e.g., on the 10th of every month) to automatically send messages to students regarding pending fees.
7. **Library Alert:** Set up automated alerts for library-related issues and specify the number of days for the alert trigger.

Business Rules:
• Automated features are designed to streamline daily operations and minimize manual intervention across various modules.

Important Notes:
• Users should have a foundational understanding of the underlying modules (voucher, payroll, analytics) to fully comprehend the impact and benefits of these automation settings.
• Automated alerts are effective tools for timely communication with students and staff regarding important deadlines and issues.

question: How can I change the display name of a field like 'Reg Number'?
answer:
This topic explains how to customize the display names of various fields and modules within the ERP to better suit the institute's specific terminology (e.g., changing 'Course' to 'Class' for schools, or 'Concession' to 'Discount'). This feature only alters the visible name, not the underlying system logic or functionality.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the section for display name customization within 'Institute Preferences'.
2. Locate the field or module whose display name you wish to change (e.g., Reg Number, Roll Number, Course, Batch, Concession, School Diary, Appreciation Certificate).
3. Enter the desired new 'Display Name' (e.g., 'Class' for Course, 'Year' for Batch, 'Discount' for Concession, 'College Communication' for School Diary, 'Transfer Certificate' for Appreciation Certificate).
4. Click the 'Save' button, typically located at the top of the screen, to apply the changes.

Business Rules:
• Only items explicitly listed in the customization section can have their display names changed.
• Changing a display name does not alter the underlying system code, functionality, or data structure; it only affects what users see on the interface.

Important Notes:
• This feature allows the ERP system to adapt to an institute's specific terminology, making it more intuitive for users.
• Ensure that the new display names are clear, consistent, and align with the institute's internal language and branding.
• For templates and certificates (e.g., Appreciation Certificate), changing the display name allows the client to use the same underlying template for different purposes (e.g., Transfer Certificate) without requiring new code.

question: How do we import our existing student data into the new ERP system?
answer:
This topic outlines the process and requirements for importing data for existing students, including their academic records, outstanding dues from previous sessions, and any applicable concessions, to ensure a smooth transition and enable fee collection in the new ERP system.

Steps:
1. Provide the ERP team with data for all existing (old) students in the specified Excel format.
2. Ensure the student data includes unique identifiers such as Admission Number and University Roll Number.
3. Submit data for any outstanding dues (pending amounts) from previous academic sessions.
4. Provide data for all existing student concessions that need to be carried forward into the new system.
5. The ERP team will then import the provided data into the system.

Business Rules:
• Each student's registration number (admission number) must be unique.
• Both the admission number and university roll number should be included in the student data.
• New admissions will be assigned a new series of registration numbers.

Important Notes:
• Importing accurate old student data is crucial for initiating fee collection and maintaining historical records.
• Detailed data on previous dues is necessary for accurate financial reconciliation.
• Explicitly sharing concession data for old students is required if these concessions are to continue in the new ERP.
• The ERP team will provide sample Excel formats to guide data submission for students, transport, and hostel.

question: What are the charges associated with using the online payment gateway (Razorpay)?
answer:
This topic addresses the charges associated with using the integrated payment gateway (Razorpay) for online transactions, including potential GST and other bank charges, and highlights the need to clarify these rates and decide on their handling.

Steps:
1. As an administrator or configurator, obtain detailed information regarding Razorpay's charges, including the base rate, applicable GST, and any other bank charges.
2. Decide whether the institution will absorb these payment gateway charges or pass them on to the student.
3. Optionally, explore and compare alternative payment gateways if the current charges are deemed uncompetitive.

Business Rules:
• Payment gateway charges are levied by the service provider (Razorpay) for facilitating online transactions.
• These charges may include GST as per government regulations.

Important Notes:
• Payment gateway charges are visible during online payment tests (e.g., during new admission registration).
• The exact rate and a detailed breakdown of these charges must be confirmed directly with Razorpay.
• The institution needs to make a clear policy decision on whether to absorb these charges or have the student bear them.
• The possibility of integrating the institution's own bank gateway or exploring other competitive options exists.

question: How do I design a custom report card with a unique layout?
answer:
This topic addresses the creation of custom templates for unique institutional requirements, such as specialized report cards or certificates with custom designs. It also covers handling complex data structures within templates and incorporating elements like images and stamps.

Steps:
1. Identify specific institutional requirements that cannot be met by default templates (e.g., unique report card layouts).
2. Design the custom template using appropriate coding (HTML, CSS, and potentially JavaScript for dynamic elements).
3. For complex reports, use the browser console to navigate through arrays and nested objects to accurately retrieve specific data points (e.g., skill groups, subjects, assessment groups).
4. Incorporate images for logos, stamps, or signatures by referencing them in the code (e.g., `DisplayData.logo`).
5. Ensure all HTML tags are properly closed to avoid preview issues and ensure correct rendering.

Business Rules:
• Some specialized reports, like pre-nursery report cards, often require fully customized designs as they are not available as default system codes.
• Stamps and signatures can be integrated into templates either by coding them directly or by embedding them as image files.
• Templates can be renamed within the system to better reflect their purpose.

Important Notes:
• The browser console for highly customized or complex reports (e.g., detailed report cards) will display a more intricate data structure with multiple arrays and nested variables.
• The template preview is a design aid; it may not accurately reflect the final print if there are unclosed tags or structural errors in the code.
• Variables for elements like institute logo (`DisplayData.logo`) or session information can be directly incorporated into the template code.

question: My student's name is not appearing on the ID card, how can I fix this?
answer:
This topic provides a guide on how to diagnose and correct issues where template variables (e.g., student name, category) are not printing correctly. It details the use of the browser's developer console to identify available data objects and their exact variable names.

Steps:
1. Print or preview the template where variables are not displaying correctly.
2. Right-click on the page and select 'Inspect' (or 'Inspect Element').
3. Navigate to the 'Console' tab within the developer tools.
4. Look for the data 'object' that contains the information being passed to the template.
5. Expand the object to view all available variables and their precise names (e.g., 'Student's name', 'Category').
6. Compare the variable name found in the console with the one used in your template's code.
7. Correct any mismatches in the template code (e.g., change `DisplayData.Student's category` to `DisplayData.Category` if that's the correct variable name in the console).

Important Notes:
• All template variables must be prefixed with `DisplayData.` (e.g., `DisplayData.EntityName`, `DisplayData.StudentName`). `DisplayData` is the array that calls and retrieves the data.
• The console for complex reports (like report cards) can be intricate, often involving nested arrays and objects for data points like skill groups, subjects, and assessment groups.
• Variable names are case-sensitive and must exactly match what is displayed in the console.

This topic provides guidance on how to diagnose and resolve issues where data variables are not correctly displaying or printing on ERP templates, using the browser's developer console to identify correct variable names.

Steps:
1. Generate or print the document where variables are not displaying correctly.
2. Right-click on the displayed document (or preview) and select 'Inspect' from the context menu.
3. Navigate to the 'Console' tab within the developer tools.
4. Locate and expand the 'Object' that contains the data for the document.
5. Identify the exact variable name required (e.g., 'Category' instead of 'StudentCategory').
6. Copy the correct variable name.
7. Edit the template code and replace the incorrect variable with the correct one, ensuring it is prefixed with 'DisplayData.' (e.g., 'DisplayData.Category').
8. Reprint or preview the document to verify the fix.

Business Rules:
• All data variables must be prefixed with 'DisplayData.' in the template code (e.g., 'DisplayData.StudentName').
• The exact spelling and case of the variable name as found in the console object must be used in the template code.
• Variables for institute information include: DisplayData.EntityName, DisplayData.EntityAddress, DisplayData.EntityState, DisplayData.EntityCountry, DisplayData.EntityPinCode.
• Variables for student information include: DisplayData.StudentGender, DisplayData.StudentName, DisplayData.StudentFatherName, DisplayData.StudentMobileNumber, DisplayData.StudentAge, DisplayData.StudentRollNumber, DisplayData.StudentSection, DisplayData.StudentStream.
• Variables for financial information include: DisplayData.TotalDemand, DisplayData.AmountPaid, DisplayData.AmountInWords, DisplayData.AmountDue.
• Other common variables include: DisplayData.PrintedBy, DisplayData.Logo, DisplayData.Session.

Important Notes:
• For complex reports (e.g., report cards), the console object might be an array containing nested variables, requiring careful navigation to find the correct path.
• Sometimes, objects are nested within arrays (e.g., for columns, positions, fee heads, installments, fee head groups), which requires specific coding to access their values.
• If a variable is not printing, it could be due to a typo in the variable name or an incorrect prefix.

question: How do I add a new bus to the ERP system?
answer:
This topic covers the process of adding new vehicles (buses) to the ERP system, including their essential details like RC number, seating capacity, and insurance information. It also explains how to update existing vehicle details.

Steps:
1. Click on the 'Settings' icon.
2. Select 'Transport'.
3. Click on 'Vehicle'.
4. To add a new vehicle: Click 'New Vehicle'.
5. Enter the 'RC number' (e.g., HR 0123).
6. Enter the 'Seating Capacity' (e.g., 50).
7. Optionally, enter 'Tank Capacity' and 'GPS ID'.
8. Enter the 'Insurance Date'.
9. Optionally, upload corresponding documents like 'Insurance Document', 'Pollution Certificate', 'Fitness Certificate', 'Road Permit', 'Road Tax'.
10. Click 'Add' to save the vehicle.
11. To update an existing vehicle: Select the vehicle from the list and click 'Update Detail' to modify its information.

Business Rules:
• RC number, Seating Capacity, and Insurance Date are mandatory fields for vehicle creation.
• Transport setup is session-dependent, meaning configurations need to be done for each academic session.

Important Notes:
• The 'GPS ID' field is used for GPS tracking systems but is not mandatory.
• The system allows for the creation of an unlimited number of vehicles.
• Vehicle details can be updated at any time after creation.

question: How do I link a vehicle in the ERP to its GPS tracking ID?
answer:
This process involves linking each vehicle in the ERP system to its unique GPS identifier provided by the vendor. This GPS ID is crucial for the system to query the correct tracking data for a specific vehicle.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Vehicles' section within the 'Transport' module.
2. Select the specific vehicle for which you want to configure GPS tracking.
3. Locate the 'GPS ID' field for the selected vehicle.
4. Enter the unique GPS ID (vendor-specific code, e.g., 'V2954') provided by the GPS vendor into the 'GPS ID' field. This value will be sent as the parameter identified by the 'GPS ID Key' defined in Track Config.
5. Save the vehicle configuration.

Business Rules:
• Every vehicle intended for GPS tracking must have its unique GPS ID configured.
• The value entered in the 'GPS ID' field for a vehicle is passed to the vendor API using the 'GPS ID Key' defined in Track Config.
• The ERP backend uses this GPS ID to fetch data from the vendor API and then matches the response using the 'Match Key' defined in Response Config.

Important Notes:
• Failure to configure the GPS ID for a vehicle will result in an error (e.g., 'GPS ID not found') when attempting to track it.
• The GPS ID is a unique identifier for each vehicle as recognized by the vendor's GPS system.
• This setup must be performed for every entity (vehicle) that requires GPS tracking.

question: How do I manually assign a transport route to a single student?
answer:
This topic explains how to manually assign a specific transport route and pick-up point to an individual student from their student profile. This process automatically links the student to the defined transport fees.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Student List'.
2. Select the desired student from the list.
3. Click on 'Detail' to open the student's profile.
4. Click on 'Assign Route'.
5. A pop-up window will appear. Select the 'Route' from the dropdown list.
6. Select the 'Pick-up Point' from the dropdown list for the chosen route.
7. The corresponding 'Amount' for the selected route and pick-up point will automatically be fetched and displayed.
8. Optionally, toggle 'Select a different route' if the drop point differs from the pick-up point route.
9. Select the 'Installment(s)' for which the transport fee should be applied.
10. Click 'Assign' to save the transport route to the student.

Business Rules:
• The system automatically retrieves the transport amount based on the selected route and pick-up point, as defined in the 'Vehicle Route' setup.
• Once assigned, the transport amount will be added to the student's fee demand for the specified installments.

Important Notes:
• This method is for assigning transport to individual students. For bulk assignments, use the 'Transport Excel Upload' feature.
• After assignment, the transport fees will be visible in the student's fee demand.

Describes the process of individually assigning a transport route and pick-up point to a student directly from their profile, which then automatically updates their fee demand with the relevant transport charges.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Student List' and select the desired student.
2. Click on 'Detail' to open the student's profile.
3. Click on 'Assign Route'.
4. From the pop-up window, select the 'Vehicle Route' (e.g., Route 1).
5. Select the 'Pick-up Point' (e.g., Ansal).
6. The system will automatically fetch and display the 'Amount' associated with the selected pick-up point.
7. The 'Drop Point' will typically be the same as the pick-up point, unless 'Select a different route' is toggled.
8. Select the 'Installment(s)' for which the transport fees should apply.
9. Click 'Assign' to save the transport details to the student.

Business Rules:
• The transport amount is automatically retrieved from the configured vehicle route and pick-up point.
• Once assigned, the transport charges will appear in the student's fee demand for the selected installments.

Important Notes:
• This method is suitable for assigning transport to individual students or making specific adjustments, in contrast to the bulk Excel upload option.

question: How can I assign transport routes to many students at once?
answer:
This topic describes how to assign transport details (vehicle route and pick-up point) to multiple students simultaneously using an Excel upload. This method is efficient for initial assignments or promoting students with similar transport arrangements.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Setup' > 'Transport' > 'Transport Excel Upload'.
2. Download the 'Sample Excel' file.
3. Prepare the Excel file with the following columns:
4.   'Reg Number' (unique student ID).
5.   'Vehicle Route' (the name of the route defined in the system).
6.   'Pick-up Point' (the name of the pick-up point defined for that route).
7. Choose the prepared Excel file from your system.
8. Click 'Submit' to upload and assign transport details to students.

Business Rules:
• Each student must have a unique 'Reg Number' for identification.
• The 'Vehicle Route' and 'Pick-up Point' names in the Excel must exactly match those defined in the system.
• Upon successful upload, the system automatically fetches and applies the corresponding transport fees to the student's demand.

Important Notes:
• This method is particularly useful for promoting students from a previous session, where transport details often remain similar. The previous session's transport report can be exported and adapted for the new session's bulk upload.
• The 'Vehicle Number' is not required in the Excel, as it is implicitly linked to the 'Vehicle Route'.

question: How do I link an ERP vehicle to its GPS tracking ID from a vendor?
answer:
This process involves linking an individual vehicle record in the ERP system to its corresponding unique identifier (GPS ID) in the external vendor's tracking system. This `GPS ID` is crucial for the ERP backend to query the vendor API for specific vehicle data and enable tracking in the application.

Steps:
1. Navigate to `Transport` -> `Vehicles`.
2. Search for the specific vehicle you wish to configure.
3. Click on the `View` option for that vehicle.
4. Locate the `GPS ID` field.
5. Enter the unique identifier (e.g., `wickle number`) provided by the GPS vendor for this specific vehicle into the `GPS ID` field.
6. Save the vehicle record.

Business Rules:
• The value entered in the `GPS ID` field must be the exact identifier that the vendor's API expects for that vehicle, corresponding to the `GPS ID Key` configured in Track Config.
• If a vehicle's `GPS ID` is not configured, tracking for that vehicle will fail in the app, resulting in an error message (e.g., 'Please contact us').
• The ERP backend uses this `GPS ID` value, passed via the `GPS ID Key` configured in Track Config, to fetch data from the vendor API.

Important Notes:
• This setup is performed per vehicle.
• The `GPS ID` field on the vehicle master is where the vendor's unique vehicle identifier is stored.

answer:

Steps:
1. Click on the 'Settings' icon.
2. Select 'Transport'.
3. Click on 'Transport Excel Upload'.
4. Download the 'Sample Excel' file provided by the system.
5. Fill the Excel sheet with student transport data, ensuring the following columns are populated:
6.   - 'Reg Number' (the unique student ID)
7.   - 'Vehicle Route' (the exact name of the route as defined in the system, e.g., Route 1)
8.   - 'Pick-up Point' (the exact name of the pick-up point as defined for that route, e.g., Ansal).

• The 'Vehicle Route' and 'Pick-up Point' names in the Excel must precisely match the names configured in the ERP system.
• Upon successful upload, the system automatically fetches and applies the corresponding transport fees to the students' fee demands based on the assigned route and pick-up point.

Important Notes:
• This feature is particularly useful for bulk assignments, such as when promoting students from a previous session where transport details often remain consistent.
• Users can export existing transport assignments from the 'Transport Report' section to use as a template for the bulk upload Excel.
• The system will generate an error file if there are any discrepancies or missing mandatory data in the uploaded Excel sheet.

question: How do I define a new transport route in the ERP system?
answer:
This topic details how to create and manage vehicle routes within the ERP system. It includes assigning vehicles to routes, defining multiple pick-up/drop points, setting timings, specifying charges, and optionally skipping transport fees for certain installments.

Steps:
1. Click on the 'Settings' icon.
2. Select 'Transport'.
3. Click on 'Vehicle Route'.
4. To create a new route: Click 'New Vehicle Route'.
5. Enter a descriptive 'Route Name' (e.g., Route 1).
6. Select the 'Vehicle' that will operate on this route from the dropdown list.
7. Optionally, select 'Skip Installment' if transport fees should not be charged for specific fee installments (e.g., June). Multiple months can be selected.
8. Optionally, select 'Employee' (driver) assigned to this route. This data comes from the HRM employee setup.
9. To add pick-up points: Enter 'Pick-up Point Name' (e.g., Ansal), 'Pick-up Time' (e.g., 6:00 AM), 'Drop Time' (e.g., 4:00 PM), and 'Amount' (e.g., 2000). Optionally, enter 'Longitude' and 'Latitude'. Click 'Add' to save the pick-up point. Repeat for additional points.
10. Click 'Add' to save the complete vehicle route.
11. To update an existing route: Select the route, click 'Edit', modify details, and click 'Update'.
12. To upload pick-up points in bulk: Click 'Upload Pick-up Point', download the 'Sample Excel', fill in the data (Pick-up Point Name, Amount, Pick-up Time, Drop Time, Longitude, Latitude), choose the file, and click 'Submit'.

Business Rules:
• Transport is session-dependent; routes may need to be re-established or copied for new sessions.
• The 'Skip Installment' feature prevents transport fees from being charged for selected installments.
• Employee data for drivers must be pre-configured in the HRM module.
• When manually adding pick-up points, Pick-up Time and Drop Time are mandatory. When using Excel upload, they are non-mandatory.

Important Notes:
• Existing vehicle routes can be copied from a previous session using the 'Copy from Session' feature.
• Longitude and Latitude fields are primarily used for integration with GPS tracking systems.
• Bulk upload of pick-up points via Excel can generate an error file if data is invalid or incomplete (e.g., missing mandatory fields).

question: How do I configure the API URL for GPS tracking in Track Config?
answer:
Track Config defines the parameters for calling a vendor's GPS tracking API, including the API URL, HTTP method (GET/POST), query parameters (e.g., tokens, extra values), request headers, and the key used to identify the vehicle in the request.

Steps:
1. **API URL:** Copy the base API URL (the part before the first '?' if present) and paste it into the 'API URL' field.
2. **Method:** Select the appropriate HTTP method: 'GET' if query patterns are sent in the URL (after '?'), or 'POST' if data is sent in an object (request body).
3. **Query Parameters:** For 'GET' requests, attach tokens or additional values required by the API. Example: `token=your_token_value`. Copy the full string (e.g., `your_token_value`) and paste it after the equals sign.
4. **Headers:** Configure the expected response format. For JSON, input 'accept' as the key and 'application/json' as the value.
5. **Request Body:** For 'POST' requests, add key-value pairs for the object to be sent in the request body.
6. **GPS ID Key (Request Parameter Name):** Copy the key name (e.g., 'vehicle_id' or 'vehicleNumber') from the vendor's documentation that the API expects as the identifier for the vehicle, and paste it into the 'GPS ID Key' field. This is the parameter name that the backend will use to send the vehicle's unique ID.

Business Rules:
• Query patterns are values appended to the URL after a question mark (?).
• POST requests send data within an object in the request body.
• The ERP backend automatically calls the vendor API based on this configuration when the internal tracking API is invoked.
• The 'GPS ID Key' in Track Config is the parameter name used by the backend to send the vehicle's unique ID to the vendor API.

Important Notes:
• This configuration needs to be set up only once.
• The 'Test Connection' feature might not always provide a response due to external API issues, but the configuration should still be completed.
• Ensure the API URL is accurate and includes all necessary base path components.

question: How are transport fees managed in the ERP system?
answer:
This topic describes how transport fees are structured, often based on routes/areas and divided into installments, and emphasizes the need for detailed transport data (bus numbers, pick-up points, student assignments) for effective management within the ERP's transport module.

Steps:
1. Provide transport fee data, including area-wise charges (e.g., 24000, 28000, 32000) and their installment divisions.

Business Rules:
• Transport fees are typically divided into multiple installments (e.g., four parts).
• Fees for transport vary based on the student's transport area or route.

• Detailed transport data, including bus numbers, pick-up points, and student divisions, is essential for the effective functioning of the transport module.
• The ERP team will provide sample Excel formats to assist in preparing transport data for import.
• The institution needs to create bus-wise divisions of children and routes if not already in place.

question: What information is required in the Excel file for student transport assignment?
answer:
This topic explains how to assign students to specific vehicle routes and pickup points in bulk using an Excel upload. This process links their transport details to their fee demands.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Setup' > 'Transport' > 'Transport Excel Upload'.
2. Download the 'Sample Excel' file.
3. Fill the Excel with the following columns: 'Reg Number' (unique student ID), 'Vehicle Route' (the exact name of the defined vehicle route, e.g., Route 1), 'Pickup Point' (the exact name of the defined pickup point, e.g., Anshal).
4. Choose the filled Excel file and click 'Submit'.

Business Rules:
• The 'Reg Number' is the unique identifier for a student in the ERP system.
• Vehicle numbers are implicitly linked through the 'Vehicle Route' and are not required in the Excel.
• Assigning transport data automatically updates the student's fee demand with the corresponding transport fees.

Important Notes:
• This option is used for bulk assignment; individual assignment might be done elsewhere (not covered in this transcript).
• Ensure 'Vehicle' and 'Vehicle Route' are already configured before assigning students.

question: Where do I find the GPS ID for a vehicle?
answer:
This process links an internal ERP vehicle record to its unique identifier from a third-party GPS tracking system, enabling live location tracking within the ERP.

Steps:
1. Navigate to the 'Transport' module.
2. Go to 'View Vehicle' and search for the desired vehicle (e.g., V2954).
3. Open the vehicle's details.
4. Locate the 'GPS ID' field.
5. Enter the unique code provided by the vendor's GPS application for that specific vehicle (e.g., V2954).
6. Save the vehicle record.

Business Rules:
• Each vehicle must have a unique GPS ID from the vendor's system.
• The GPS ID must be configured for the vehicle to appear on the track wall/map in the ERP app.
• If the GPS ID is not configured, an error 'GPS ID is not found' will be displayed.

Important Notes:
• The value entered in the 'GPS ID' field is passed to the backend, which then uses the configured Track Config and Response Config to fetch and display live tracking data.
• This setup is crucial for enabling the 'Track Vehicle' functionality in the ERP app.

question: How do I define a new transport route for a bus?
answer:
This topic explains how to define specific routes for each vehicle, including associated pickup/drop-off points, timings, and charges. It also covers options for copying routes from previous sessions and bulk uploading pickup points.

Steps:
1. Navigate to 'Institute Setup' > 'Transport' > 'Vehicle Route'.
2. To create a new route, click 'New Vehicle Route'.
3. Enter a 'Route Name' (e.g., Route 1).
4. Select the 'Vehicle' (bus) assigned to this route from the dropdown.
5. (Optional) Use 'Skip Installment' to exclude transport charges for specific fee installments.
6. To add pickup points manually:
7. Click 'Add Pickup Point'.
8. Enter 'Pickup Point Name' (e.g., Anshal).
9. Enter 'Pick Up Time' (e.g., 6:00 AM).
10. Enter 'Drop Time' (e.g., 4:00 PM).
11. Enter the 'Amount' (charge) for this pickup point (e.g., 2000).
12. (Optional) Enter 'Longitude' and 'Latitude' for GPS tracking.
13. Repeat for additional pickup points.
14. To upload pickup points in bulk:
15. Click 'Upload Pick Up Point'.
16. Download the 'Sample Excel' file.
17. Fill the Excel with 'Pickup Point Name', 'Amount', 'Pick Up Time', 'Drop Time'. (Pick Up Time and Drop Time are non-mandatory in Excel).
18. Choose the filled Excel file and click 'Submit'.
19. Click 'Save'.

Business Rules:
• Vehicle routes are session-dependent.
• The 'Copy from Session' feature allows replicating routes from a previous academic session.

Important Notes:
• An error file will be generated during bulk upload if mandatory information (e.g., amount) is missing in the Excel.
• Longitude and Latitude are used for GPS tracking systems.

question: How do I create a new vehicle route in the system?
answer:
This topic details how to define bus routes, assign vehicles to routes, specify pick-up and drop points with their respective timings and charges, and manage the skipping of transport fees for specific installments. Routes can be created manually or copied from previous sessions.

Steps:
1. Navigate to Settings icon > Transport > Vehicle Route.
2. To create a new route, click 'New Vehicle Route'.
3. Enter a 'Route Name' (e.g., Route 1).
4. Select the 'Vehicle' that will operate on this route from the dropdown list.
5. Optionally, select 'Skip Installment(s)' if transport fees should not be charged for particular installments (e.g., June).
6. Optionally, select 'Employee(s)' (drivers) to assign to this route. This data comes from the HRM employee setup.
7. Add 'Pick-up Points':
8. Enter the 'Pick-up Point Name' (e.g., Ansal).
9. Enter the 'Pick-up Time' and 'Drop Time' for this point.
10. Enter the 'Amount' associated with this pick-up point.
11. Optionally, enter Longitude and Latitude for GPS tracking integration.
12. Click 'Add' for each pick-up point.
13. Click 'Add' to save the complete vehicle route.
14. To copy routes from a previous session, click 'Copy from Session' and select the desired academic session from the dropdown.
15. To update an existing route, select the route from the list, click 'Edit', make the necessary changes, and click 'Update'.
16. To upload pick-up points in bulk, click 'Upload Pick-up Point', download the sample Excel file, fill it with the required data, choose the file, and click 'Submit'.

Business Rules:
• Transport setup is session-dependent.
• The 'Skip Installment' feature allows excluding transport fees for selected installments (e.g., June for schools).
• Employee data (drivers) must be pre-configured in the HRM employee setup.
• Pick-up Time and Drop Time are non-mandatory when uploading pick-up points via Excel, but are mandatory when adding them manually.

Important Notes:
• The 'Copy from Session' feature is highly useful for entities where transport routes remain largely consistent across academic sessions.
• Longitude and Latitude fields are primarily for integration with GPS tracking systems.
• Bulk upload via Excel is an efficient method for adding numerous pick-up points to a route. The system will generate an error file if there are invalid entries during the upload process.
• You can add multiple pick-up points to a single route.

question: How do I add a new bus or vehicle to the system?
answer:
This topic explains how to set up the transport system, including adding vehicles, defining vehicle routes, specifying pickup and drop points, and assigning drivers. It also covers how to manage session-dependent transport data and assign routes to individual students.

Steps:
1. To add a new vehicle: Navigate to 'Transport' -> 'Vehicle', then click 'New Vehicle'.
2. Enter mandatory vehicle details: RC Number, Seating Capacity, and Insurance Date. Optionally, add Tank Capacity, GPS ID, Insurance Company, and upload related documents (Pollution Certificate, Fitness Certificate, Road Permit, Road Tax). Save the vehicle.
3. To create a vehicle route: Navigate to 'Transport' -> 'Vehicle Route'. (Optional: To copy routes from a previous session, click 'Copy from Session' and select the desired session.)
4. Click 'New Vehicle Route'. Enter a 'Route Name' (e.g., Route 1) and select the 'Vehicle' (bus) that runs on this route.
5. Optionally, select 'Skip Installment' for months when transport fees should not be charged (e.g., June).
6. Select the 'Employee' (driver) assigned to this bus route from the list.
7. To add pickup points for the route: Click 'Add Pickup Point'. Enter 'Pickup Point Name', 'Pickup Time', 'Drop Time', and the 'Amount' (fee) for that point. (Optional: Enter Longitude and Latitude for GPS tracking.) Click 'Add' to save the pickup point. Repeat to add multiple pickup points.
8. Alternatively, pickup points can be uploaded in bulk via Excel using the 'Upload Pick Up Point' option and a sample Excel template.
9. Save the vehicle route.
10. To assign a route to an individual student: Navigate to 'Student List', select the desired student, and click 'Assign Route'.
11. In the pop-up window, select the 'Route' and 'Pickup Point'. The amount will be automatically fetched. (Optional: Toggle 'Select different route' if the drop point differs from the pickup point.)
12. Select 'All Installments' or specific installments for which the transport fee should apply. Click 'Assign'.

Business Rules:
• Transport setup is session-dependent, meaning the setup needs to be done for each academic session.
• Mandatory fields for vehicle addition include RC Number, Seating Capacity, and Insurance Date.
• Transport fees can be skipped for specific installments (e.g., June in schools).
• The system automatically fetches the transport amount based on the selected route and pickup point.
• Employee data (drivers) must be added in the HRM module before they can be assigned to routes.

Important Notes:
• The 'Copy from Session' feature for vehicle routes is useful for entities with similar transport setups across sessions.
• GPS ID, Tank Capacity, Longitude, and Latitude are optional fields, primarily for GPS tracking integration.
• When assigning a route to a student, the system automatically adds the transport fee to the student's demand for the selected installments.

question: How do I assign a transport route to an individual student?
answer:

Steps:
1. To add a new vehicle: Navigate to 'Transport' -> 'Vehicle', then click 'New Vehicle'.
2. Enter mandatory vehicle details: RC Number, Seating Capacity, and Insurance Date. Optionally, add Tank Capacity, GPS ID, Insurance Company, and upload related documents (Pollution Certificate, Fitness Certificate, Road Permit, Road Tax). Save the vehicle.
3. To create a vehicle route: Navigate to 'Transport' -> 'Vehicle Route'. (Optional: To copy routes from a previous session, click 'Copy from Session' and select the desired session.)

5. Optionally, select 'Skip Installment' for months when transport fees should not be charged (e.g., June).
6. Select the 'Employee' (driver) assigned to this bus route from the list.
7. To add pickup points for the route: Click 'Add Pickup Point'. Enter 'Pickup Point Name', 'Pickup Time', 'Drop Time', and the 'Amount' (fee) for that point. (Optional: Enter Longitude and Latitude for GPS tracking.) Click 'Add' to save the pickup point. Repeat to add multiple pickup points.

question: What is the difference between positive and negative tags?
answer:
This topic explains how to effectively manage admission leads using tags, follow-ups, and the various features available on the Admission Leads page, including filtering, global search, and direct communication tools.

Steps:
1. To add/manage Admission Tags:
2. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Tags.
3. 2. Click 'Add New Details'.
4. 3. Enter the desired tag name (e.g., 'Interested', 'Not Interested').
5. 4. Choose a color combination for the tag.
6. 5. Select 'Positive' if the tag should trigger a follow-up, or 'Negative' if it should trigger a remark.
7. 6. Save the tag.
8. To create 'Duplicate' and 'Duplicate Primary' tags (special case):
9. 1. For 'Duplicate' tag:
10.    a. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Tags.
11.    b. Click 'Add New Details'.
12.    c. Enter 'Duplicate' (ensure no leading/trailing spaces).
13.    d. Choose a random color.
14.    e. Mark as 'Negative' and save.
15.    f. Edit the tag, change its hex value to '000000' (black) and save.
16. 2. For 'Duplicate Primary' tag:
17.    a. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Tags.
18.    b. Click 'Add New Details'.
19.    c. Enter 'Duplicate Primary'.
20.    d. Select any color.
21.    e. Mark as 'Positive' (generally) and save.
22.    f. Edit the tag, change its hex value to '000000' (black) and save.
23. To apply a tag and add a follow-up/remark to a lead:
24. 1. On the Admission Leads page, select a lead.
25. 2. Based on the conversation, select a respective tag (e.g., 'Interested', 'Not Interested').
26. 3. If a positive tag is selected, the system will prompt to add a follow-up (date, time, remark).
27. 4. If a negative tag is selected, the system will prompt to add a negative remark.
28. 5. Update the lead.
29. To filter leads on the Admission Leads page:
30. 1. By default, 'Not Engaged' and 'Engaged with Pending Follow-up' statuses are ticked.
31. 2. By default, only positive tags are selected.
32. 3. To view leads with negative tags, manually select the specific negative tag from the filter options.
33. 4. To view all leads regardless of tag, use the 'Global Search' option and enter the application number.
34. To perform actions on a lead:
35. 1. On the Admission Leads page, select a lead.
36. 2. Options include: Add Follow-up, Add Visit (record campus visit), Add Note, Make Calls (requires IVR integration), Check Timeline (view lead history), Open WhatsApp (direct communication via WhatsApp Web).

Business Rules:
• Positive tags trigger a follow-up prompt (date, time, remark).
• Negative tags trigger a negative remark prompt.
• Leads with no activity are marked with red ribbons ('not engaged').
• By default, the Admission Leads page only shows leads with positive tags and 'Not Engaged' or 'Engaged with Pending Follow-up' statuses.
• Duplicate leads are automatically marked by the system if the same configured field (e.g., mobile number) is used again.
• 'Duplicate Primary' tag identifies the first lead created with a specific number/field.

Important Notes:
• Ensure no leading or trailing spaces when creating the 'Duplicate' tag name for proper system functionality.
• IVR integration is required for direct calling functionality from the leads page.
• The 'Open WhatsApp' feature automatically opens WhatsApp Web with the student's number pre-filled.

question: How do I categorize my lead sources?
answer:
This topic details the backend setup for admission management, including defining lead sources and source groups, configuring automatic lead assignment to counselors using round robin, setting up duplicate lead detection fields, and structuring admission teams for data visibility.

Steps:
1. To add/manage Admission Sources:
2. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Sources (implied).
3. 2. Add new sources (e.g., Website, Social Media, Walk-in).
4. To create Admission Source Groups:
5. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Source Groups (implied).
6. 2. Create a new group (e.g., 'Organic', 'Inorganic', 'Third Party Vendors').
7. 3. Assign relevant individual sources to each group.
8. To configure Counselor Mapping (Round Robin Assignment):
9. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Counselor Mapper.
10. 2. Select specific courses or sources for which to map counselors.
11. 3. Select multiple counselors to be assigned leads from the chosen courses/sources.
12. 4. Choose the Round Robin assignment type:
13.    a. All: System balances lead load among counselors. If a new counselor joins, they receive leads until their count matches existing counselors, then assignment proceeds one-by-one.
14.    b. Devise: System assigns leads one-by-one to all active counselors, regardless of current lead count. New counselors are included in the rotation immediately.
15. To set up Duplicate Field Master:
16. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Duplicate Field Master.
17. 2. Select the field(s) (e.g., Phone Number, Aadhaar Card, Roll Number) on which the system should check for duplicates.
18. 3. Save the configuration.
19. To configure Admission Team Structure:
20. 1. Navigate to Admission Setup > Admission Master > Admission Team.
21. 2. If a single senior person manages multiple counselors without distinct teams, delete any existing team structures and save.
22. 3. If there are distinct teams (e.g., Domestic, External):
23.    a. Create a new team (e.g., 'Domestic Team').
24.    b. Assign a Team Lead.
25.    c. Add team members (counselors) to the team.
26.    d. Repeat for other teams.

Business Rules:
• Source groups combine individual sources for consolidated reporting.
• Counselor mapping automatically assigns leads based on selected courses/sources using a round robin method.
• 'All' round robin balances lead distribution, while 'Devise' assigns sequentially.
• Duplicate Field Master determines which fields trigger duplicate lead detection.
• Team leads can view data of their team members; team members cannot see each other's data.
• Senior-most persons can see data of sub-teams.
• If a counselor is part of multiple teams, their data is visible to all respective team leads.

Important Notes:
• The 'All' round robin type ensures an even distribution of leads over time, prioritizing new counselors or those with fewer leads.
• The 'Devise' round robin type ensures immediate inclusion of new counselors in the lead assignment rotation.
• Carefully consider the team structure as it impacts lead visibility and reporting.
